title: Wgpu Renderer Full Parity
description: Bring the wgpu renderer (framework/renderer/wgpu, ui/wgpu, infinite/world) to full visual and functional parity with the React reference renderer (framework/renderer/react). Scope: restore compile after ViewState locale/terminology schema change; close the five open wgpu tickets (window options chip z-order, render plan validator, lowpoly dev boot, world3d empty preview, 3d component hover/select/edge-preview); implement the three placeholder-only componentScene surfaces (puzzle2d-board, icon-render, note-canvas); shell parity sweep (presence overlay, dead code cleanup); extend the wgpu playground e2e harness to compare against React reference screenshots and produce a parity report across all ~30 playgrounds.
summary:
Implemented the `icon-render` componentScene surface in the wgpu-native renderer, closing one of the three placeholder-only surfaces in scope for this ticket (puzzle2d-board and note-canvas were completed by concurrent sessions on the same ticket during this work).

Added `SurfaceKind::IconRender` to `render_component_scene`'s dispatch table in framework/renderer/wgpu/rs/lib.rs (previously fell through to the bare placeholder). Threaded a new `icon_render_states: HashMap<String, infinite_world::World3dState>` map through `render_ui_node`/`render_ui_node_inner`/`render_component_scene`, `ShellState` (field + `new()` init), and the two `render_ui_node` call sites in the shell's render paths — mirroring the existing `world3d_states` plumbing pattern, but deliberately excluded from all orbit-camera pointer/wheel/dispatch routing in `AppRuntime` (icon-render is a static, non-interactive preview, not an orbit viewport).

`render_icon_render` (new `//#region IconRender`) parses `IconRenderScene.request_json` (camera position/target/fov/zoom/up, GLB assetUrl, lights, width/height/shape/background/material), synthesizes a `World3dScene` from it — folding the three.js `zoom` factor into an equivalent vertical FOV since the native orbit camera has no independent zoom, building a single mesh/instance entry from the GLB URL via the existing `world3d_mesh_id_from_url`/`world3d_meshes_json_from_urls` helpers, and populating `environment_json` from the request's lights/material/background/shadow fields — then delegates the actual GPU draw to the existing `infinite_world::render_world_3d` into an aspect-fit sub-rect of `bounds` computed from the request's width/height (matching the React host's CSS aspect-fit framing). On top it paints 2D DrawList chrome: an accent-colored aspect-fit border, a `{width}×{height} · {shape}` badge (bottom-right, matching `IconShotFrame`'s badge in the React reference), the `footer` string (bottom-center), and a "No shot" empty state when the request is missing or fails to parse (mirroring `icon-render-host.tsx`'s empty state).

Extended `AppRuntime::poll_pending_assets` (both the native blocking branch and the wasm async branch) to also drain pending GLB fetches from `icon_render_states`, not just `world3d_states`, so icon-render's GLB actually loads instead of staying a placeholder box forever.

Added a `shooting-wgpu-dev` entry to `.claude/launch.json` (port 6120, `SEMIO_RENDERER=wgpu`, reusing the `dev:shooting:base-icon` fixture) alongside the existing `shooting-react-dev` reference entry, following the established wgpu-dev grouping/naming convention, for future comparison against `SEMIO_RENDERER=react`.

Verified: `cargo check -p semio-framework-renderer-wgpu` compiles cleanly (the crate briefly failed to compile mid-session due to unrelated, concurrent in-progress note-canvas work from another session on the same file/ticket — resolved itself once that work landed, unrelated to this change). `cargo test -p semio-framework-renderer-wgpu --lib` (30/30 passing) and `cargo test -p infinite_world --lib` (25/25 passing) both green.

Not verified: live visual comparison against SEMIO_RENDERER=react in the browser — the session's 5-dev-server preview slot pool was fully occupied by other concurrent chat sessions for the duration of this work, and the dev explicitly chose to skip visual verification rather than wait further. The `shooting-wgpu-dev` launch config is in place and ready for a follow-up visual check whenever a preview slot is available.
